items.stem: Explain why resolving forces in two perpendicular directions is enough to find the resultant of several coplanar forces.

items.answer: (a) weight vertically down, normal reaction perpendicular to the plane, P horizontal (b) P = 9.33 (c) 22.1 N
items.markingKey: (a) B1 all three forces [1] (b) M1 P cos θ = mg sin θ; A1 P [2] (c) M1 resolves perpendicular to the plane; A1 R [2]

items.stem: A particle of mass 10 kg rests on a smooth plane inclined at 35°. Find the component of its weight down the plane.
items.markingKey: mg sin α.

items.stem: Omar says that, for a particle of mass 8 kg on a smooth plane inclined at 35°, the normal reaction equals the weight, 80 N. Explain the error.
items.answer: Only the perpendicular component of the weight is balanced by R: R = mg cos α = 65.5 N.
items.markingKey: B1 resolves perpendicular to the plane; B1 correct R [2]

items.stem: A particle slides down a smooth plane inclined at α, where sin α = 3/5. Ana says its acceleration is g cos α = 8.00 m s⁻². Explain the error.
items.answer: The component of the weight down the slope is mg sin α, so a = g sin α = 6.00 m s⁻²; g cos α is the perpendicular component.
items.markingKey: B1 sin for the component along the slope; B1 correct value [2]

items.stem: A particle is released from rest on a smooth plane inclined at α, where sin α = 3/5. Find its speed after it has travelled 8 m down the plane.
items.markingKey: M1 a = g sin α; A1 a; M1 v² = 2as; A1 speed [4]

items.stem: A particle of mass 10 kg is pulled up a smooth plane inclined at 10° by a force of 30 N acting up the line of greatest slope. Find its acceleration and the normal reaction.
items.markingKey: M1 P − mg sin α = ma; A1 a; B1 R [3]

items.stem: A particle of mass 8 kg is pulled from rest up a smooth plane inclined at 15° by a force of 100 N parallel to the line of greatest slope. The force is removed after 3 s. (a) Find the normal reaction. (b) Find the speed of the particle when the force is removed. (c) Find the further distance the particle moves up the plane after the force is removed.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 mg cos α [1] (b) M1 a; A1 v = at [2] (c) M1 speed at removal; M1 deceleration g sin α; A1 distance [3]

items.stem: A force of 20 N acts at 30° above the horizontal. Find its horizontal component.
items.markingKey: Horizontal component = 20 cos 30°.

items.stem: A resultant force has components 3 N in the x-direction and 4 N in the y-direction. Ethan gives its direction as tan⁻¹(4/3) = 53.1° from the positive x-axis. Explain why this may be wrong and give the correct direction.
items.answer: tan⁻¹ ignores the quadrant: the force points into the first quadrant, so the direction is 53.1° from the positive x-axis.
items.markingKey: B1 identifies the quadrant; B1 correct angle [2]

items.stem: A force of 20 N acts at 55° to the horizontal. Ana gives its horizontal component as 20 sin 55° = 16.4 N. Explain the error.
items.answer: The horizontal component is adjacent to the 55° angle, so it is 20 cos 55° = 11.5 N.
items.markingKey: B1 cosine for the adjacent side; B1 correct value [2]

items.stem: Forces act on a particle: 12 N at 120° anticlockwise from the positive x-direction; 20 N in the negative y-direction. Find the magnitude of the resultant force and the angle it makes with the positive x-direction.

items.stem: Three horizontal forces act on a particle of mass 4 kg resting on a smooth horizontal surface: 12 N in the negative y-direction; 8 N at 210° anticlockwise from the positive x-direction; 15 N in the negative x-direction. (a) Find the magnitude and direction of the resultant force. (b) State the fourth force that would keep the particle in equilibrium.
items.answer: (a) 27.1 N at −143.9° to the positive x-direction (b) 27.1 N at 36.1° to the positive x-direction
items.markingKey: (a) M1 Pythagoras; A1 magnitude; A1 direction [3] (b) B1 equal and opposite to the resultant [1]

items.stem: A particle of mass 8 kg hangs from a string and is held in equilibrium by a horizontal force of 20 N. Find the tension in the string.
items.markingKey: Tension balances the weight and the horizontal force: T = √(W² + P²).

items.stem: A particle of weight 20 N hangs in equilibrium from two strings inclined at 35° and 70° to the horizontal. Show that the tension in the first string is 7.08 N, correct to 3 significant figures.
items.answer: Resolving: T₁ cos 35° = T₂ cos 70° and T₁ sin 35° + T₂ sin 70° = 20; solving gives T₁ = 7.08 N.
items.markingKey: M1 resolves both ways; A1 solves to the given value [2]

items.stem: A particle of weight 100 N hangs in equilibrium from two strings inclined at 30° and 25° to the horizontal. Ravi assumes each string has tension 50 N. Explain why this is wrong.
items.answer: Only the vertical components of the tensions support the weight, and the strings are at different angles; resolving gives T₁ = 111 N and T₂ = 106 N.
items.markingKey: B1 components, not tensions, balance the weight; B1 correct tensions [2]
